official_measurement_examples.name: Wild-bird protection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states all wild birds are protected, including nests in use or being built and their eggs, with additional protection for Schedule 1 birds.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning standing advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Wild-bird standing advice is a material planning consideration and developers should provide evidence on avoidance or mitigation where birds may be affected.

official_measurement_examples.name: No development licence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states there are no wild-bird licences that allow development proposals or construction; developers must comply with the legal protection through avoidance and lawful exemptions where applicable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Active nest protection
official_measurement_examples.fact: Damaging or destroying a nest while it is in use or being built can be an offence, independent of whether planning permission exists.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 GL41 scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: GL41 is a 2026 general licence for specified public-health or public-safety purposes and is not a development licence.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 GL42 scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: GL42 is a 2026 general licence for specified serious-damage purposes and cannot be treated as a general construction licence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Individual licence purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: A08 or A09 individual licences are available for defined control purposes where general or class licences do not cover the action, not simply because a development has planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Wild-bird compliance does not itself grant planning permission, prove absence of nesting birds or establish parcel development capacity.

core_rules: wild-bird protection law is not proof birds are present on a parcel
planning permission does not remove active-nest protection
wild-bird standing advice is not a planning decision
there is no general wild-bird development or construction licence
GL41 public-safety licence is not development permission
GL42 serious-damage licence is not development permission
CL12 air-safety licence is not a general development licence
A08 or A09 licence is purpose-limited and not a planning substitute
historic bird survey must retain its date and season
absence of a recorded nest is not proof no active nest exists
bird habitat duty does not determine land ownership
licence conditions must be tied to actual species purpose and dates
wild-bird compliance does not reserve development capacity
bird protection compliance does not create access rights
no parcel wild-bird clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
